title: [Suite autour de Teichmüller dont] Teichmülleries, 1981-1982 : notes manuscrites (1981-1983, s.d.), lettres (1981, s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page carries only a diagram, page IV of a series of figures. In ink it shows a three-dimensional lattice of groups, essentially a cube (in fact a 3x4x2 grid) with three kinds of arrows. Hooked arrows are injections. Arrows labelled '2' are almost certainly index-2 inclusions, or extensions or quotients of order 2. Arrows labelled 'σ' go to the groups written in gothic S (𝔖, 𝔖⁺), which look like symmetric or permutation groups (possibly their even or 'positive' parts). That reading makes σ the homomorphism recording how a mapping class permutes marked points or boundary components. Dashed arrows give alternative or non-canonical maps, or identifications between two copies of the same group placed at different corners (Π̲⇢Π̲, 𝔖̲⁺⇢𝔖̲⁺, N^?_ρ⇢N^!_ρ).

The objects fit Grothendieck's 1981-82 'Teichmüllerian' bookkeeping for small modular groups:
- M, M', M'' and their decorated variants M^!, M^?, M^{!!}_0, M^?_0 are versions of a mapping-class (Teichmüller modular) group. The decorations ', '', !, ? appear to switch between extended (orientation-reversing allowed) and orientation-preserving versions, and between versions with and without a centre or marking.
- Π, Π̲, Π̲_0, Π_{τ'} look like (orbifold) fundamental groups or their index-2 subgroups.
- μ, μ_{τ'} are central subgroups of order 2 (μ_2, plausibly an elliptic or hyperelliptic involution).
- D_{τ'}, D_ρ look like dihedral-type groups; N_ρ, N^?_ρ, N^!_ρ like normalisers of a finite subgroup ρ.
- Z^!_ρ and Z^!_{0ρ} = M(j̄) look like centralisers. M(j̄) suggests the stabiliser in the modular group of a special point (an elliptic point, cf. j = 0, 1728) or of an involution j̄.

Each horizontal row reads like an extension chain 'finite subgroup ↪ normaliser/centraliser ↪ ambient modular group →σ permutation group', for example 1 ⇢ μ̲ ↪ Π̲ →σ 𝔖̲⁺ and Z^!_ρ ↪ M'' →σ M'. The other two directions encode passing to index-2 subgroups. This gives a compatible 3-parameter system of short exact sequences.

The faint pencil draft below is an earlier version of the same lattice. It has extra nodes N_ρ, Z_ρ (struck), D_ρ and L_ρ, and the corner N^?_{ρ0} is already struck out. In ink, N^?_{ρ0} and N^!_{ρ0} are struck through, so Grothendieck removed the 'ρ0' normaliser corner as redundant or incorrect.

The next page begins listing ST_{0,2}, ST_{1,1}, ST_{1,2}. That suggests the cube serves a case analysis of low-dimensional surface types (g,n) and their 'special' points with extra automorphisms, i.e. the finite-subgroup / orbifold-point structure of the Teichmüller tower near genus 0 and 1. The previous sheet is a reused scrap of a 1979 thesis notice and gives no mathematical context.
errors: No verifiable error. Without definitions on the page, the exactness and commutativity of the cube cannot be checked.
Grothendieck himself struck out the corner nodes N^?_{ρ0} and N^!_{ρ0}, in both ink and pencil. This signals that this part of the configuration was abandoned or judged wrong.

ideas.what: A three-dimensional commutative lattice of group extensions relating mapping-class groups, centralisers/normalisers of finite subgroups, index-2 (orientation) variants and permutation actions on marked points.
ideas.modern_name: Extended vs. orientation-preserving mapping class groups; normalisers/centralisers of finite subgroups (stabilisers of orbifold points of moduli space); the forgetful map to the symmetric group of punctures
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard mapping class group theory (Birman, Harvey, Maclachlan–Harvey on finite subgroups/branch loci, Kerckhoff/Nielsen realisation)
ideas.where_published: Related themes (Teichmüller tower, low-dimensional modular groups as building blocks) appear in Esquisse d'un programme (1984), but not this diagram.

ideas.what: M(j̄) = Z^!_{0ρ}: the centraliser of an involution or special element identified with a modular-type group.
ideas.modern_name: Stabiliser of an elliptic/special point in the modular group (e.g. in GL2(Z)/PGL2(Z))

deep.surprise_reason: This is a bookkeeping diagram of group-theoretic relations among small Teichmüller modular groups and their finite-order symmetries, with no text. It records nothing that is not standard, beyond showing how carefully Grothendieck organised the index-2 and σ variants.
transcription_corrections: The arrow labels are '2' (index-2 maps) and 'σ'. The machine's double-headed arrows (←→, ↔) are mostly hooked injections in the image, with the hook end at the source.
Top row in ink: N^?_{ρ0} (struck) ←2→ N^!_ρ ⇠ N^?_ρ ↪ M^? →σ M. The second struck node, slightly lower and set back, is N^!_{ρ0}.
The left column also has M^!_0 / M^?_0, and M^{!!}_0 ↪2 M'', with vertical '2' arrows connecting the levels.
Bottom-front row: Π̲_0 ↪2 Π̲, with Π̲ →σ 𝔖̲⁺ drawn as a diagonal arrow down to a separate 𝔖̲⁺ node at the bottom.
Middle row: μ_{τ'} ↔2 D_{τ'} ↔ Π_{τ'} ↔σ 𝔖.
The pencil draft contains Z_ρ (possibly struck) and L_ρ in place of Π, and D_ρ next to D_{τ'}.
The page number at bottom left is 140; the archive sequence is page 139.
